summary: Laurent Van Cutsem is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, KU Leuven, and Ghent University, where he earned his doctorate in 2023 and became Doctor-Assistant (2023–2026).

Laurentios Myriantheus was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Rizarios Ecclesiastical School and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Munich, studying under Martin Haug and Wilhelm von Christ.

Laurie L. Patton is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Harvard and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1991). She held professorships at Emory and Duke, and served as president of Middlebury College (2015–2024) and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (~2024).
Lavanya V. Eswar is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Lawrence Cohen, working in Indology and other fields, received a Doctor of Pharmacy from the University of Southern California (1979). He served as professor and chair at Washington State University (2002–2012) and at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2026).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He served as a director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as a professor of theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Epstein is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied at UCLA, George Washington University, VA West Los Angeles Medical Center, and Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, later serving as assistant professor at the University of Washington (attested 1999–2001).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was an Indologist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at NYU, Virginia Theological Seminary, Oxford, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, becoming a professor at the University of Oxford in 1897.

Lawrence J. McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who studied under Sheldon Pollock. Attested as a professor at Cornell University in 2026, his students include James McHugh and Whitney Cox.

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Butler, Indiana, NYU, the International Academy of Merchandising and Design, Northwestern, Santa Fe University, St. John's, and earned a doctorate from the California Institute of Integral Studies.
Laxmanshastri Joshi (1901–1994) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati (~1916–1923) and served as director of Prajna Pathashala from ~1955 to 1994.
Laxmidhar Behera works in computational fields and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur and the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi.

Lazăr Șăineanu (1859–1934) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bucharest, the University of Paris, and Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1889). He worked under scholars including Haşdeu, whom he temporarily substituted for at Bucharest (1890–1892).

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

LeRoy Carr Barrett (1877–1960) was an Indologist who studied at Washington and Lee and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held academic posts at Johns Hopkins (1903–1907), Princeton (1907–1909), Dartmouth (1909–1910), and Trinity College (from 1910).
Leah Judith Zahler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Harvey B. Aronson, and Geshe Wangyal.

Lee Jonathan Chilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed an MPhil at the University of Sydney (2002–2024), where he also held an alumni/executive post in 1998, and undertook studies at several other institutions.

Lee Ling Ting is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees from the University of Adelaide (BA), Peking University (MA), and Harvard University (PhD), and was a postdoctoral fellow at Vassar College in 2024.
Lee Yearley is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and sinology. He held a professorship at Stanford University (attested 1989–1992) and later became emeritus there (attested 2026).

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. Attested in 2011, he served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus, at Drew University and as a research associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.
